title: Cache Geometry Under Obfuscation
subtitle: Per-head rotation does not hide SVD features, and a KV-Cloak implementation is inconclusive (v1.1 correction)
abstract: Version 1.1 (October 2026) withdraws this paper's claim that KV-Cloak defends cache-geometry methods against adversaries. Per-head orthogonal rotation, the simulation of KV-Cloak used throughout, leaves the singular-value features that cache-geometry detectors read unchanged: in a 100-prompt replication none of the 24 cross-head features moved, and a classifier scored AUROC 0.994 with and without the rotation. An implementation of the full KV-Cloak mechanism reduced the best detection feature from AUROC 0.903 to 0.614 on 7 confabulations, while two other features were no lower than without it; at this size the data cannot show whether detection survives.
